title: Deterministic Verification with a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Sealed Paired Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent reused for both episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the confirmatory estimand reported here applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition that was run. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the run manifest referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps) to produce device CLI sequences from operator intent. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional changes. The community response often composes a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that interposes a deterministic validator and, when permitted, bounded automated repair between generation and acceptance. Prior surveys and empirical studies document that LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled setups while leaving nontrivial verifier-detectable defects [1],[2], and that GVR-like architectures reduce mechanically checkable errors in code and configuration domains [3],[4].

This work asks a focused, preregistered question: when the same initial LLM candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), what is the marginal verifier-detected improvement of inserting a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair? That estimand isolates only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs and avoids conflating effects due to differing first-pass generations across arms. We executed the registered confirmatory synthetic/emulation partition with N_pairs = 250 constrained NetOps intents generated deterministically, invoked a single shared initial gpt-5-mini generation per intent, applied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 to guarded episodes, allowed up to one automated template-driven repair when validation failed, and then analyzed paired binary outcomes with an exact McNemar test and paired-bootstrap CI.
sections.related_work: Several recent surveys and applied studies examine LLMs for NetOps and the role of verification. NetConfEval and other NetOps evaluations show feasibility of intent-to-configuration pipelines on emulated tasks but emphasize remaining syntax/semantic gaps [1],[2]. Tooling and verification research (e.g., Batfish evolution, Plankton, header-space approaches) provide mature deterministic checks for forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[5]. Work on generate-and-verify and program-repair in code and configuration domains shows measurable increases in mechanically verifiable correctness but also documents limits where semantic correctness requires richer tests or human oversight [4],[6]. Security analyses of prompt-injection emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers but note adaptive adversaries remain an open threat [7]. Our contribution differs by using a sealed, preregistered paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics and by publishing the exact reconciliation counts and stage accounting for generation and repair, enabling reproducible audit of the marginal validator effect on identical candidates.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the evidence bundle). The confirmatory estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics with N_pairs = 250. The preregistered analysis specified an exact two-sided McNemar test for the paired comparison and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break, all-down-before-change). Tasks intentionally exercised medium→very_hard dependency patterns to stress ordering and group-activity invariants; task manifest and representative payloads are archived in the run manifest.

Model invocation and shared_initial_candidate semantics. For each intent we produced exactly one initial model-generation call with declared model gpt-5-mini. That single generated candidate was reused for both episodes in the pair (baseline: accept candidate; guarded: validate candidate). The preregistration allowed up to one automated repair call per episode; repair templates were constrained to syntactic and ordering fixes (reordering to match required_sequence, splitting multi-command lines, canonicalizing tokens). The execution adhered to this single-repair policy.

Deterministic validator and scoring rule. The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: parse CLI, count parsed_command_count, check required_sequence and workflow constraints, construct an expected_final_state snapshot from the task payload, and return normalized_configuration and boolean valid. The primary outcome is validator.valid for each episode (binary). Exclusion rules removed episodes failing vendor-parser deterministically or containing denylisted/private tokens; none were excluded in this run.

Analysis. The primary analysis used an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired outcomes (n10 vs n01) and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples). Missingness and contamination sensitivity plans were preregistered; no confirmatory episodes were excluded or flagged in the executed partition.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run completed planned_episode_count = 500 (250 pairs), completed_episode_count = 500, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-stage accounting reconciles to stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250 and repair = 1 (one repair call exercised across the whole run). These counts reflect the shared_initial_candidate design: a single initial generation per pair plus a single repair generation in the guarded flow.

Primary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (1.000). The paired contingency table is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair corresponds to the only exercised repair and represents a repair conversion rate of 1/250 = 0.4% for the confirmatory partition.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] in absolute proportion (0.0–1.2 percentage points). These numeric artifacts and the contingency CSVs are archived in the run manifest.

Representative validator diagnostics. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count encoded in task payloads; for example, a representative hard task (task-000003) parsed six commands and satisfied the expected_final_state snapshot in both episodes. The only failing baseline candidate corrected by the single permitted repair involved a command-ordering/normalization issue that the template-driven repair resolved; the repair trace is archived.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational meaning. Under the constrained synthetic/emulation partition and shared_initial_candidate semantics, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of a deterministic validator plus one automated repair was small: an observed paired improvement of 0.4 percentage points with an upper 95% bound of 1.2 percentage points. Artifact-grounded drivers of this small effect include (i) constrained and deterministic task generation that reduced ambiguity in intents and allowed_touched_fields, (ii) a capable LLM (gpt-5-mini) producing well-formed CLI sequences for these constrained tasks, and (iii) deterministic validators that check mechanically verifiable properties and therefore cannot capture richer behavioral or protocol-level correctness.

Power and assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N = 250 to detect a 15 pp effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) was substantially higher than assumed, reducing sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements; the paired-bootstrap CI is therefore the most informative summary of plausible verifier improvement under these conditions.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: dependence on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, and the shared_initial_candidate design; results measure only marginal validator+repair effect on identical candidates. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 captures syntax, ordering, and snapshot constraints but not live protocol dynamics or emergent multi-device behaviors. External validity: the executed confirmatory partition is synthetic/emulation only; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised and remain open threats.

Implications. These findings do not imply validators or repairs are unnecessary in broader operational deployments. Rather, they quantify a narrow margin under favorable emulator-style conditions and a single-repair policy. Validators that check richer invariants, multi-iteration repair policies, multi-model ensembles, or adversarial testing could materially increase observed benefits in other settings.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus a single automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intents, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed deterministic validation in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We emphasize that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand pertains only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and discoverable via the run manifest indicated in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted automated repair, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model used for initial generation = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded in execution manifest), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, and adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The executed guarded flow permitted at most one automated, template-driven repair per episode as specified by the preregistration. Execution accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation calls + 1 repair), with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} documented in the run manifest.

Preregistration and immutable master prompt: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration artifact archived). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Artifact bundle and manifest pointer: the full execution and analysis bundle (raw model responses, task manifest, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, analysis CSVs, and a full hash manifest) is archived together; the run-level manifest file within the bundle is execution/execution_manifest.json and provides the complete per-artifact index and checksums for auditors. Readers and reviewers should consult that manifest for full machine-verifiable artifact mappings. The confirmatory estimand reported here was executed only on the synthetic/emulation partition; the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run (explicit deviation disclosed).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) but did not measure live protocol dynamics, emergent multi-device interactions, or broader semantic correctness.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.

Realized baseline pass-rate (0.996) substantially exceeded the preregistration assumption (~0.90), reducing power to detect small absolute improvements; the paired-bootstrap CI bounds are therefore the most informative summary under these realized conditions.
